prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the seated camera wearer looking down at their own lap and hands (brightest, ~0.2–0.6 m away), with a rectangular metal tray of shelled peas resting on their thighs (~0.5 m) between chair armrests, while a small wooden side table to the upper left and a cushioned sofa to the upper right lie farther away (~1.0–1.8 m, separated by ~0.5 m of floor at ~1.5–2.0 m). No other people are present in the scene, and the wearer's hands, lap tray, and a blue plastic bag of pea pods are all within direct arm's reach while the surrounding furniture is just beyond normal reach and partly cropped at the frame edges. Across the five frames, the blue bag starts on the left thigh in frames 1–2 (~0.5 m), is lifted close to the camera in frame 3 (~0.2–0.3 m) where it occludes the tray and lap, and is moved across to the right side (~0.5–0.7 m) in frames 4–5 as the camera view rotates slightly rightward. The depth map clarifies the vertical separation between the raised hands/bag, the tray surface, and the recessed floor more distinctly than the flat overhead RGB perspective. However, it looks unreliable during the fast motion in frame 3—where the blurred bag and hands merge into an indistinct white blob—and it washes out fine 3D details like individual peas and small objects on the distant table and sofa.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to capture almost the entire room layout, omitting the furniture, floor, blue plastic bag, and the camera wearer's body in frames 1–3 and 5, while only detecting isolated foreground regions on the wearer's lap at ~0.4–0.6 m distance. Specifically, it detects the pile of green peas on the tray in frames 1, 2, and 4 (within arm's reach in front of the wearer), two overlapping masks on the metal tray around the peas in frame 4, and a single mask on the wearer's left forearm at the bottom-center of frame 5 (~0.4 m away), with no other people present or facing the camera. Across the sequence, all detections vanish completely in frame 3 when the moving blue bag occludes the tray, reappear on the tray and peas on the lower left in frame 4 after the bag moves right, and reduce to just the left forearm in frame 5. While the sharp mask contours in frames 1, 2, and 4 help isolate the spatial boundary of the piled peas from the reflective metal tray, this map is highly unreliable: it misclassifies shelled peas as 'broccoli' and the flat rectangular tray as two overlapping 'bowl' instances, misses the peas entirely in frame 5, and fails to segment the wearer's hands, legs, or any background furniture.
descriptions.pose: The pose map displays only 2D magenta hand skeletons against a completely black background, providing no spatial information about the room layout, furniture, objects, or any other people (as only the camera wearer is present, facing downward toward their lap). In frame 1, only the wearer's right hand is detected (~0.4–0.5 m from the camera, lower-left of the strip's first frame), and in frame 2 only the left hand is detected grasping the bag on the left (~0.4–0.5 m), with both hands operating within immediate arm's reach above the lap while the rest of the wearer's body remains out of view or undetected. The skeletons disappear completely in frames 3 and 4 during the rapid lifting and rightward transfer of the blue bag, then reappear in frame 5 as a single skeleton for the left hand resting near the tray edge (~0.4 m, center-left) while the right hand holding the bag on the far right goes undetected. The articulated finger keypoints in frames 1, 2, and 5 make the exact flexion and orientation of the curled fingers clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is very unreliable overall, missing all yellow body keypoints (wrists/forearms/thighs) across all frames, dropping one hand in frames 1, 2, and 5, and failing to detect either hand in frames 3 and 4 due to motion blur and self-occlusion with the plastic bag.
